correctness.rationale: The normalizations are explicit: full-sphere probability measure, orthant mass 2^{-d}, pure degree-two homogeneous tracefree forms, and Euclidean isometry scaled by d(d+2). Direct Dirichlet quartic moment formula covers all monomial patterns and yields the exactly stated quadratic form. The unsigned incidence matrix BB^T=(d-2)I+J diagonalizes into one constant-edge, d-1 standard 2x2, and d(d-3)/2 null-edge sectors, exhausting the dimension. Positivity of the 2x2 determinant follows from pi>3; strict location of alpha between the eigenvalues follows from pi<22/7, and top branch dominance is algebraic. Analytic large-d limiting expansions give the sharp constant. Degree-one formula independently follows from two conditional second moments. Standalone code built full gamma-moment Gram matrices for d=3..12 and passed 399 checks, but numerical tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Full text of the 2004 Simons–Dahlen–Wieczorek spherical Slepian article and 2021 Michel–Plattner–Seibert manuscript was materially compared to the precise result. Those sources formulate arbitrary-region concentration matrices and polar-cap techniques, but not the all-dimensional evaluated orthant pure-quadratic four-sector spectrum, sharp ordering, unique top mode or quadratic-in-d sharp condition number. The matrix framework is prior and credited; its evaluated orthant solution requires a nontrivial fourth-moment/incidence spectral reduction and an exact inequality involving pi. Searches for positive orthant, hyperoctant, spherical simplex, coordinate sign chamber, octant and Gram eigenspectra returned no demonstrably equivalent theorem. Existing hemisphere, lune, signed coordinate-cap and full-sphere moment statements concern distinct regions or functionals and do not force the orthant spectrum. The conclusion is provisional: an implicit older symmetry-moment formula remains plausible.
residual_risks: An older symmetric-group tensor/moment identity could implicitly diagonalize the same orthant kernel even if it does not use Slepian terminology.
No independent historian or mathematical expert has validated originality.
Related Roddy–McEwen paper was not inspected page-by-page; no negative coverage conclusion is based solely on its abstract.

value.rationale: The spherical positive orthant is the canonical reflection-chamber spherical simplex. Its second-degree harmonic spectrum is a naturally motivated exact invariant for tomography from a non-axisymmetric portion of a sphere. Classifying all four eigenvalue sectors and extremizers, proving subtle strict ordering, and identifying the exact d^2 growth of the concentration-condition ratio versus d growth for degree one gives a new structural stability separation. This is not a renamed textbook inequality, an arbitrary numerical slice, or a claim of broad optimality.
